description:
Plan: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-exceptions.html, decision 1 (kinds), ticket 3.

Build: delivery carries kind error | throw | exit. Kernel gains throw/1 and exit/1 (never), reraise/2 (re-raises an exception with a stacktrace argument that is accepted and ignored). catch heads: one head catches throws only; two heads catch kind, value with guards allowed; `catch :error, r` binds the raw value without wrapping. rescue never matches throw or exit. Uncaught throw prints `** (throw) <value>`; uncaught exit prints `** (exit) <reason>`; both exit 1 from main, except exit(:normal), exit(:shutdown), exit({:shutdown, n}) which follow the Elixir CLI (status 0, 0, n) and print nothing.

Acceptance (interp, run, build; elixir oracle):
- throw caught by one-head catch; by `catch :throw, v`; guard on kind (`catch k, v when k == :throw`).
- `catch :exit, r` catches exit/1; rescue alone lets a throw and an exit propagate to an outer catch.
- uncaught throw and uncaught exit lines and status; exit({:shutdown, 7}) status 7 with nothing printed.
- reraise/2 inside a rescue reaches the outer rescue with the same exception.
- a throw in a spawned process prints its line and main continues.
- unit tests for the kind tag in delivery and the status mapping.
- exceptions doc gains kinds and the CLI status table; lib/kernel.fz docs for throw/exit/reraise.
- gate green as in the epic.
title: throw, exit and catch are kinds on the same handler stack
